subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram partial-stream finalization lacks clear delivery-mode observability (sent vs preview-finalized vs canceled)

question: Should this fix be limited to explicit Telegram final-delivery logs/events, or should it change the delivery confirmation boundary so session state is not treated as delivered until Telegram send/edit success is proven?
rationale: The issue asks for observability, while the discussion and linked PR move toward stronger delivered-state semantics that affect fallback behavior and may overlap the broader cross-channel delivery contract.

options.title: Confirm Delivery Boundary
options.body: Require Telegram partial-stream finals to mark delivered only after all send/edit work succeeds, and expose the final outcome for operators.

options.title: Limit To Observability
options.body: Add explicit final-mode logs or events while preserving current session delivered-state behavior.

options.title: Defer To Cross-Channel Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open but let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561 settle the durable delivery contract first.

recommendation.title: Confirm Delivery Boundary
recommendation.body: Require Telegram partial-stream finals to mark delivered only after all send/edit work succeeds, and expose the final outcome for operators.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans Telegram delivery semantics, fallback behavior, and broader channel delivery contracts where recent adjacent history makes this the best available routing owner.
